segments.title: 第150章 翻紅的征兆
segments.content:
Reigniting the Verdant Years Chapter 150: Signs of a Resurgence

After returning home at night, Li Luo specifically opened QQ Music on his computer to check the comments for the song "Annual Rings."

After reading them, his expression twitched. He didn't know whether to be speechless, or to feel fortunate and happy to have such "lovely readers."

Then a thought occurred to him. He recalled the question Yan Zhusheng had asked him during the day, whether more people had been reading his book lately.

With a mind to investigate, Li Luo clicked open his author dashboard and then opened the data panel.

It clearly showed that the total number of collections for his current book was 50,317.

In other words, a total of over fifty thousand people had added the book "I'm Really Not a Star" to their bookshelves.

But based on his current average subscription of just over three thousand, in reality, only one reader out of every dozen or so chose to pay for the official subscription and read the entire book.

The remaining readers were either letting the book accumulate chapters or just went straight to pirated versions.

Even so, readers who knew to look for books on a legitimate source like Qidian were still in the minority.

A very large portion of the web novel readership probably had no idea a place like Qidian even existed.

They might have even always thought that web novels were free to read, and thus had been finding and reading books on pirate sites from the very beginning.

And under these circumstances, Li Luo glanced at his work's daily report, where he could see the daily increase in collections for his book.

Starting from December 1st, the growth, which had originally been a natural increase of one or two hundred per day, suddenly surged to 1,500.

In the three days that followed, the increases were 2,800, 1,700, and 2,100, respectively.

This was what had caused his total collections, which were just over forty thousand, to surge to fifty thousand.

Taking another look at the average subscription, Li Luo raised an eyebrow.

Before this, after the average subscription for "I'm Really Not a Star" had risen to 3,700, it had stagnated.

In November, his editor, Qian Zhou, had arranged a promotional spot for him on the main page, which successfully pushed his average subscription past 4,000, but then it stalled again.

And in the recent short span of three or four days, his average subscription had actually reached 4,500.

This left him somewhat astonished.

But then, he looked up news related to "Yaochi Immortal Love."

The first stop was Weibo.

As the main hub for the traffic economy, it was obvious that after a TV series starring a "little fresh meat" idol went online, Weibo would be the most important front for publicity.

Back at the end of last month, in the first few days after "Yaochi Immortal Love" was released, the hot search topic about the "little fresh meat" idol Tong Hua starring in "Yaochi Immortal Love" had already been on the trending list for quite a while.

On the day of the premiere, this topic shot straight to the top, and along with it, several other pieces of news related to "Yaochi Immortal Love" also temporarily made it onto the hot search list.

The online discussion was incredibly heated.

Although most of the comments in the QQ Music comment section were complaints about the plot, it was a completely different story on Weibo.

Weibo was a sea of positivity.

Everywhere you looked, girls were squealing and fawning over Tong Hua, madly cheering for their idol, and meticulously finding every possible angle in the TV series to praise him.

Li Luo didn't know if these were real people or an army of bots directed by Huayue Media, but he figured the numbers were heavily padded.

But at least from the data alone, it was clear they had made thorough preparations.

However, if one were to search carefully, they could still find reviews from regular viewers who weren't fans of the "little fresh meat" idol.

Especially from some bloggers who specialized in reviewing films and TV series. The ones who wrote serious reviews were basically all complaining about the show's cringeworthy aspects.

For example, the most classic issue in female-oriented stories: the plot seems to involve the fate of a nation and deep-seated feuds, but in the end, the actual focus of the story always lands on the romantic entanglements between the female lead and several male leads.

The plot of the series "Yaochi Immortal Love" was actually very simple.

The female lead was originally an ordinary lotus growing in the Yaochi of the Celestial Realm. After a long time, it gained spiritual awareness and was enlightened by a certain immortal in charge of Yaochi, successfully taking on a human form.

Yes, this immortal was the second male lead.

Gentle, humble, and proficient in all four arts: zither, Go, calligraphy, and painting.

After transforming, the female lead stayed by his side, living a carefree life every day in Yaochi.

Until one day, the Demon Realm invaded, Yaochi was cast down into the mortal world, and the female and second male leads were forced to separate.

The reason the Demon Lord of the Demon Realm, who was the first male lead played by "little fresh meat" Tong Hua, attacked the Celestial Realm, seemed on the surface to be the conflict between immortals and demons, but in reality, he was specifically targeting Yaochi.

He was after the ten-thousand-year-old white lotus nurtured by the immortal waters of Yaochi, which could revive the dead and regrow flesh from bone.

In other words, the female lead's original form before she transformed.

The second male lead saw through the Demon Lord's goal, so when Yaochi fell to the mortal realm, he used his powers to send the female lead away.

In order to find the female lead, this white lotus, the Demon Lord also chose to enter the mortal world to search for her.

What followed was a story of you-chase-I-flee, of loving and hating each other, and finally falling in love. The Demon Lord couldn't bear to use the female lead as a medicinal ingredient to cure a chronic illness from his demonic cultivation, and in the end, chose to die.

But then the female lead, having fallen in love with the Demon Lord, willingly sacrificed her life to revive him.

The Demon Lord, holding the now-dead female lead, roared at the heavens, turned the entire Celestial Realm upside down, and demanded to know if there was any divine medicine that could bring her back to life.

Well... the plot hadn't progressed that far yet, but out of curiosity, Li Luo had previously asked Luo Fei for the series outline of "Yaochi Immortal Love." After reading it, he had an expression that was hard to describe.

How should he put it... it perfectly fit his stereotype of female-oriented stories.

Especially in this kind of xianxia series, the romance between the male and female leads was the most important thing. All matters of good and evil had to queue up far behind the leads' relationship.

But it had to be said, this kind of plot was incredibly potent against young girls who hadn't seen much of the world, or even older aunties.

But likewise, male viewers who were dragged into watching this series by their female friends were filled to the brim with the desire to complain.

The only bright spot in the entire series was the song "Annual Rings," sung by Yuan Wanqing.

As a result, many people gathered on QQ Music for solidarity and to vent their complaints.

What many of them hadn't expected was that the song "Annual Rings" was actually an original creation by a novel author.

And it wasn't from the same novel as the original work of "Yaochi Immortal Love."

This piqued the interest of quite a few people.

However, most of these people ended up on pirate websites. The ones who actually came to Qidian to read the official version accounted for the few hundred new average subscriptions from the past few days.

At this rate, he didn't know how long this level of growth would last.

After figuring out the series of connections here, Li Luo was both amused and exasperated.

He never thought that "Annual Rings," a song he had written in his book by a strange twist of fate, would explode with such energy a few months later, to the point where it could even boost his novel.

At this thought, Li Luo felt a little tempted.

After all, he still had several recorded songs, like the two he sold to Yuan Wanqing. He figured if the opportunity arose in the future, they might appear on her new album.

If he was lucky and a similar wave of traffic came again, and he could write these two songs into his novel, wouldn't there be more to gain?

But…

If he did that, the fact that he was writing a novel would probably no longer be a secret to some of the people around him.

Li Luo sighed. He was truly in a difficult situation.

He would just take it one step at a time.

It wasn't like he was short on money for the time being.

Last month's royalties had been calculated, totaling over twenty thousand yuan.

Including the income from selling the songs, Li Luo now had more than three hundred thousand yuan in savings in his bank account.

To be honest... in his previous life, even by the age of 35, Li Luo had never saved up so much money at once.

He never imagined that after being reborn, only a few months had passed, and he had already achieved financial freedom as a high school student.

As Li Luo was thinking about this, he heard a knock on the door behind him.

Ying Chanxi, who had just finished her shower, peeked her head in. With her long, wet hair, she said to Li Luo, "Help me dry my hair."

"Come and sit down."

In a private room of a restaurant downstairs from the Huayue Media building.

Yuan Wanqing and Luo Fei had arranged to meet for a late-night meal. With a slightly worried look on her face, she shared what happened at the meeting during the day with her best friend.

"So Zhai Senlei wants you to stop commissioning songs so casually? At the very least, every request has to go through his approval first?" Luo Fei sneered. "Is he pretending the contract doesn't exist?"

"After all, the last album didn't perform well, so I can understand why he'd say that." Yuan Wanqing shook her head and said, "But..."

"What are your thoughts?"

"It's just... how do I put it." Yuan Wanqing's expression was a little lost. "Didn't you tell me to check the comment section for 'Annual Rings' today?"

"Uh-huh." Luo Fei nodded. "Didn't you also go read the novel Li Luo wrote?"

"But that's not the point." Yuan Wanqing smiled helplessly. "You should check my Weibo."

"Before the new album was released, I had about 200,000 followers."

"After the new album came out, the company helped me manage it up to 1 million, but the real increase was only a few tens of thousands."

"But since 'Yaochi Immortal Love' started airing, less than a week has passed, and my follower count has already grown to 1.2 million."

"This time, there was no help from the company. It's all organic growth."

"Huh?" Luo Fei was clearly stunned for a moment. "What do you mean? How did it increase like that?"

"Um... I didn't understand at first either. Later, I realized it might be because of this video." Yuan Wanqing opened her phone and showed Luo Fei a screen recording of a variety show.

On it was Yuan Wanqing with the main cast of "Yaochi Immortal Love," participating in a variety program.

Yuan Wanqing was basically just a side character on the show, only getting to sing a couple of lines from the chorus of "Annual Rings" midway through.

But it was this very clip, after being screen-recorded and shared by netizens, that inexplicably went viral on Weibo.

A netizen summarized it.

Everything else in this episode is trash. The only highlight is Yuan Wanqing's voice.

By comparison, Sister Qing is a breath of fresh air.

What's this song? It's pretty good.

The theme song for the new series "Yaochi Immortal Love." Of course, I'm not recommending the series to you. Just listen to the song, and whatever you do, don't watch the show!

Thanks, I got curious and went to watch it. I've been poisoned to death and am in urgent need of Sister Qing's "Annual Rings" to cure me.

Luo Fei blinked as she read these comments, taking a moment to process it all.

After a long while, Luo Fei looked at Yuan Wanqing and suddenly said, "What did I tell you before? Opportunities can come at any time. You have to seize this one."

"How am I supposed to seize it?"

The question Yuan Wanqing asked that night.

Received its answer the very next day.

"Sister."

The next morning, just as Yuan Wanqing was enthusiastically browsing Li Luo's novel, her assistant ran into the studio and said to her excitedly:

"Several variety shows want to invite you to participate."

"They don't have any other special requests, they just want you to go on stage and sing 'Annual Rings.'"

(End of Chapter)
